title: Workload probe and request-coalescing policy stitcher (profiling, heuristics, continuous params)
creator: Marta Ruiz
description: Build a continuous workload-probing service and a policy-stitcher that translates observed request signatures into safe, incremental request-coalescing (batching + prefix cache) recommendations and automated, guarded config applies. The output should be conservative by default, produce human-readable suggested diffs, run a shadow evaluation, and support one-click staged rollout with automatic health-based rollback.
background: We've seen uneven latency/cost tradeoffs across customers due to static batching settings. Existing offline heuristics miss short burst patterns and prefix reuse opportunities. This ticket aims to create a live probe that builds workload signatures, an offline simulator to validate candidate coalescing params, and a policy composer that emits guarded changes consumable by the runtime apply pipeline.
goals: Continuously profile production request characteristics (sequence lengths, prefix reuse, inter-arrival times, KV hit rates)
Generate ranked, explainable coalescing parameter recommendations (microbatch size, max-latency, prefix-cache window, KV ttl)
Provide a shadow evaluation harness that computes expected cost delta and 95th/99th p90 latency impact
Enable safe automated apply with canary/staged rollout and deterministic rollback signals
scope: Implement workload probe, signature store, recommendation engine (heuristic + simple ML baseline), simulator for expected cost/latency, and integration hooks into the existing rollout controller. Add UI endpoints for suggestions and acceptance diffs.
out_of_scope: Full ML model for predictions (follow-up), global autoscale actuator, and UI polish beyond minimal accept/reject flows.
acceptance_criteria: Probe collects signatures from at least three production cohorts and stores them in the signature store
Recommendation engine produces top-3 candidate parameter sets with an explainability summary
Simulator can run shadow evaluation on historical traces and produce cost & latency delta estimates within +/-10% of actual when applied in a canary
Rollout controller can apply a staged change (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and auto-roll back if error rate or p99 latency increase exceeds configured thresholds
Documentation (playbook) exists describing safe-apply knobs and emergency rollback steps
technical_approach: 1) Lightweight probe agent embedded at edge routing layer to emit anonymized signatures (no PII) to the signature store. 2) Signature aggregation job that builds workload fingerprints daily and computes candidate param heuristics based on observed prefix reuse and inter-arrival distributions. 3) Simulator: replay sampled traces in a containerized runtime with adjustable params to estimate cost and tail latency. 4) Policy stitcher: synthesize patch diffs for runtime batching configs, annotate with confidence and rollback triggers. 5) Integrate with rollout controller to support shadow eval, staged apply, and automatic rollback. Implement conservative default thresholds and human approval gates for high-risk customers.
data_requirements: Sampling policy (1:1000) for high-throughput customers, anonymized fields: model_id, route, token_count, prefix_hash, kv_hit_boolean, timestamp. Retention: 14 days for raw traces, 180 days for aggregated signatures. Access controls: probe data goes to internal analytics bucket with KMS encryption.
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal test tenants -> Beta: 3 pilot customers with infra team oversight -> Gradual: opt-in for low-risk customers with default canary schedule (10%/50%/100%) over 48 hours. Monitor cost per token, request success rate, p99 latency. Collect feedback and adjust heuristics.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: error rate +5% absolute or p99 latency +25% relative sustained for 5 minutes. Manual rollback via console 'revert recommendation' button. All applies produce a reversible diff stored in the audit log; runbook ‘batching-emergency-rollback.md’ linked.
testing_plan: Unit tests for signature aggregation, end-to-end shadow evaluation on replay traces, blue/green and staged apply in staging environment, chaos test (inject artificial inter-arrival jitter), and an offline A/B simulation comparing suggested params to current baseline.
risks: Over-aggressive recommendations could increase tail latency for bursty routes
Insufficient sampling may miss periodic patterns (daily spikes)
Data privacy/regulatory constraints for customers in certain regions
Simulator mismatch: synthetic replay might not fully capture multi-tenant queueing effects
mitigations: Conservative defaults + human approval for high-impact changes
Shadow evaluation and small canaries before full apply
Per-customer opt-out and region-aware sampling policies
Calibrate simulator using canary actuals and improve model iteratively
dependencies: infra/signature-store migration (ops ticket) - storage and encryption
console API for accept/reject suggestions (PM work)
notes: 2025-02-14: Spike completed. Prototype probe agent emits prefix_hash + token_count. Initial results show 7% average prefix reuse across sampled routes.
2025-02-20: Discussed heuristics with runtime team. Decided to prioritize prefix-cache window and microbatch cap over speculative KV TTL changes for rollout 1.
2025-02-25: UX sync - console will show explainability table and a one-click 'apply with canary' action. PM requested explicit confidence score in suggestions.
2025-02-28: Shadow evaluation run on 7 days of trace produced estimated cost savings of 12% for pilot customer A, with simulated p99 latency +3% (within acceptable bounds).
2025-03-01: Security review intake submitted for probe data flow (pending). Preparing pilot infra for three customers next week.
